title: Explainable AI‐based strength and sustainable material evaluation of lightweight nano‐concrete reinforced with hybrid basalt, polypropylene, and groundnut waste fibers
content:
Abstract

The demand for sustainable, high-performance construction materials has driven the development of lightweight nano-concrete systems that balance structural strength with environmental responsibility. Conventional mix-design approaches rely on empirical methods and provide limited insight into hybrid fiber interactions. This study proposes an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework to assess the strength and sustainability of lightweight nano-concrete reinforced with hybrid fiber composites comprising Basalt Fiber (BF), Polypropylene (PP) fiber, and Nano Groundnut Waste Fiber. Groundnut fiber serves as an eco-friendly reinforcement, while BF and PP fibers enhance tensile strength, crack resistance, and durability. The framework integrates experimental analysis with interpretable machine learning models to predict compressive, tensile, and flexural strengths, along with sustainability indicators such as density reduction and thermal efficiency. Experimental results show that the optimized hybrid mix achieved a maximum compressive strength of 85.2 MPa at 56 days, with significant improvements in tensile and flexural performance. The XAI model demonstrated high predictive accuracy (94.6%), with a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.96023 and an Adjusted R 2 of 0.92183. The hybrid system achieved a 7.5% weight reduction and reduced thermal conductivity (1.28 W/m·K), indicating enhanced sustainability. XAI techniques provide interpretability by quantifying the influence of fibers and nano-additives, reducing trial and error in mix design. The results confirm improved strength-to-weight efficiency and sustainability, supporting intelligent and eco-friendly construction applications.
